obs: “The term corporation as used in the acts of Congress touching internal revenue does not include a State, consequently the income of the State of Georgia … has not been made by law a subject of taxation. Again, The term person as used in 9 and 44 does not include a State.”
Dollar Savings Bank v. United States

"It is a familiar principle that the King is not bound by any act of Parliament unless he be named therein by special and particular words. The most general words that can be devised ... affect not him in the least, if they may tend to restrain or diminish any of his rights and interests."

"The term \"person\" as here used applies to natural persons, and also to artificial persons, bodies politic, deriving their existence and powers from legislation, but cannot be so extended as to include within its meaning the Federal government. It would require an express definition to that effect to give it a sense thus extended."
"it was a rule of construction that 'the King is not bound by any act of Parliament, unless he be named therein by special and particular words.'"

"the general rule is stated in Chitty on the Law of the Prerogatives of the Crown, 382, clearly to be' that though the king may avail himself of the provisions of any acts of Parliament, he is not bound by such as do not particularly and expressly mention him. For it is agreed in all our books that the King shall take benefit of any act, although he be not named."
"Respondent invokes the canon of construction that a sovereign is presumptively not intended to be bound by its own statute unless named in it"
“Since, in common usage, the term person does not include the sovereign, statutes employing the phrase are ordinarily construed to exclude it.”
United States v. United Mine Workers of America
"There is an old and well-known rule that statutes which in general terms divest pre-existing rights or privileges will not be applied to the sovereign without express words to that effect."
United States v. United Mine Workers of America
"The Act does not define persons. In common usage that term does not include the sovereign"
Federal Power Commission v. Tuscarora Indian Nation
"A general statute imposing restrictions does not impose them upon the Government itself without a clear expression or implication to that effect."
Examining Bd. of Engineers, Architects and Surveyors v. Flores De Otero
“the absence of any indication in the language, purposes, or history of 1983 of a legislative intent to include the District within the scope of its coverage, supported the Courts conclusion.”

"The word person for purposes of statutory construction, unless the context indicates to the contrary, is normally construed to include corporations, companies, associations, firms, partnerships, societies, and joint stock companies, as well as individuals. 1 U. S. C. 1."
“[I]n common usage, the term 'person does not include the sovereign, [and] statutes employing the phrase are ordinarily construed to exclude it.”
